questions.q: What does 'health' mean beyond not falling sick?
questions.a: Full physical, mental and social well-being - feeling fit, happy and getting along with others.

questions.q: Name two things besides medicine that keep us healthy.
questions.a: Balanced food, clean water, exercise, rest and hygiene.

questions.q: How does community health differ from personal health?
questions.a: Community health covers clean surroundings, safe water and disease control for all, not just one person.

questions.q: How does clean water protect health?
questions.a: It keeps water-borne diseases like cholera and typhoid away.

questions.q: Why is exercise part of staying healthy?
questions.a: It keeps muscles, heart and lungs strong and helps the body fight illness.
Daily bathing and hand-washing before meals (also brushing teeth, trimmed nails).

concepts.title: Knowing We Are Unwell: Symptoms and Diagnosis

questions.a: A sign of disease the patient feels or shows - fever, cough, rash, headache.

questions.q: Why do doctors ask many questions before diagnosing?
questions.a: Symptoms point to causes; the pattern helps identify the disease and choose treatment.

questions.q: Name two symptoms that suggest a stomach infection.
questions.a: Vomiting and loose motions (often with stomach ache and fever).

questions.q: How are diseases classified by how long they last?
questions.a: Acute diseases end quickly (cold, flu); chronic ones last long (TB, diabetes).

questions.q: Give one example each of infectious and non-infectious disease.
questions.a: Infectious: malaria. Non-infectious: high blood pressure (or scurvy).
Germs - bacteria, viruses, fungi, protozoa - spreading through air, water, food or insect bites.

questions.q: Name two ways to prevent infectious diseases.
questions.a: Vaccination and keeping surroundings clean (safe water, hygiene, mosquito control).

questions.q: How does a mosquito net or repellent protect health?
questions.a: It stops mosquitoes that carry malaria and dengue from biting.

questions.q: Why do we boil or filter drinking water?
questions.a: Boiling kills germs and filtering removes them, making water safe from water-borne disease.
